doc.title: Mr. and Mrs. A.C. Synigal Interview, 1962-05-24

title: Billy Kersands on the showboats and the diamond from the queen
summary: Mr. Senegal recalls Billy Kersands' showboat troupe in New Iberia, Bunk Johnson's band playing for him, and his trip to England.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Well, I wanted to ask you about Billy Kersan. How did he happen to come to Donaldson's then?
Where, where was he from? I don't know.
I think Billy Kersan came from Donaldson then. Did he?
Yeah.
I heard that. He did? Yeah. Billy Kersan came from Donaldson. Billy Kersan used to ride those steamboats. They had, they had shows on those. What you used to call those shows again?
Night shows. I mean, showboats.

Showboats. Showboats. Showboats. They used to travel from one bayou, one section to another. I remember when Bill Kersan came to New Iberia on a showboat. And I'm trying to think of the name of that boat. And they had, he stayed there, I think it was almost a week. You see. And went out, came in to buy a, to buy the food, to buy a tash. You see. Into buy a tash from a Tuffle out there. They went to buy a tash and he made several shows at New Iberia and St. Martinville, I think, and Franklin, and Patterson. And he made shows. And he sang and he had a troupe with him. He was like a santa had a troupe. I just remember how many of them were in the troupe by now. But he had a troupe and he had ladies in there too singing, you know. And he had a band. He had a brass band. What you call that a brass band? Yeah. Everything was brass band. I've heard several people talk about him. I know Bunk played with it. Yeah.
Yeah. Yeah. Bunk played with it.

Bunk played with it. Yeah. Bunk Johnston played carnette with him. Bunk Johnston played carnette in that band. In fact, Bunk Johnston was a band leader. I don't remember what that was. And Bunk Johnston's band played for Billika Sam. Billika Sam didn't play music. But he sang. He used to sing.
Said a lot of jokes.
And he'd make mouth with it. And he'd tell you remember when he'd open his mouth and be that big. See? And he'd make everybody laugh. Oh, right.
Yeah.

And Bunk Johnston made a trip to, let me see, something rich farmer. I think. Fine-ass. And sent him to England. Billika Sam made a trip to England. And when he went to England, he's the first man in history that made Queen Elizabeth laugh. She never laughed all her days. She never laughed. Oh my gosh. She never would laugh. No matter what you see, she never laughed. But the first man Billika Sam made her laugh. Billika Sam made her laugh.
Billika Sam made her laugh.

She gave Billika Sam a big diamond. And that's $5,000 at that time that diamond was worth. That big he was wearing on his chest. Yeah. From Queen Elizabeth. I think it's Queen, yeah. Queen Elizabeth. Is it Elizabeth or Victoria?
Either one. Was it?
Queen Elizabeth or Queen Victoria? I don't know. I think you're right. I think I'm wrong. I think it's Queen Victoria. Oh, yes.
I think it is Queen Victoria.

I'm a little off on that, I think. That sounds like the right, but I can't remember which it's with. Yeah, well I got mixed up myself on that. I think she's right. I think it is Queen Victoria. I've heard people talk about him and there's a book that has something about Billy Kershaw. Yeah, lots about Billy Kershaw. Well, I saw him. I saw him. I saw him. And Billika Sam is the first person that ever made her laugh during her whole lifetime for childhood. And when he opened his mouth, she didn't laugh. And she, boy, he's mother. And he put on a show out the world. She gave him that great big diamond, you know. There was a talk about that diamond for years after, until now. Remember that big diamond that Queen Victoria gave Billika Sam. And that he was the first one that ever made her laugh. She never laughed, even from a child, she never laughed. No matter how funny or how common.
I interviewed anybody who spoke of Billika Sam. Oh, yeah.
Charlie Love played trumpet with him. He's from Flagler. Oh, yeah. He lives in Algiers now. But he told us about him and said that he could put a whole cup in salsa.
Yeah. In his mouth. Yeah, that's right. Oh, he had the biggest mouth you ever seen in my life.
